To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fluctuations of the adsorbed film thickness are well described by a Gaussian distribution, and that the corresponding mesoscopic Hamiltonian has a simple form that can be used to predict, with high accuracy, the probability distribution of the film thickness.

we have found a simple Hamiltonian for the mesoscopic fluctuations of the adsorbed liquid films that is consistent with the theoretical prediction by Parry and co-workers and that it is able to describe accurately the fluctuations observed in our Monte Carlo simulations of Lennard-Johns liquid films.

the fluctuations of adsorption layers of a Lennardo-Jones liquid on a planar wall can be described by a mesoscopic Hamiltonian with a functional form that is very close but not identical to that predicted by density-functional theory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Hamiltonian for the mesoscopic fluctuations of wetting films, H[ξ], is a function of a single dimensionless parameter, the ratio of the wall-fluid and the fluid-fluid interaction strengths, and the functional form of H[ξ] is universal for the class of systems that we have analyzed.

the mesoscopic description of the fluctuations is not a universal property of a given fluid-wall combination.
